doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Sun Ra's hippie and beatnik audience
summary: Audiences were mostly young white bohemians; Sun Ra also used poetry and singing at venues like Café Wha?.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Homogenized is a good word. Can I ask if you recall on the live gigs you played if he attracted a mostly white audience or a mostly black audience?
Yeah. He what? It was mostly a white, young Bohemian hippie audience. You remember those days? You’re probably too young.
No I remember. It wasn’t in my spirituality though just yet.

Young hippie or the beatnik crowd. You remember the beatnik crowd? And they would smoke hashish, hashish and LSD at that time was big. LSD, hallucinogenics, they were big at that time. Actually peyote too. Peyote and hashish, those were the drugs of the hippies. But they called themselves elite, you know what I mean, back in those days. I’m talking about the 50s and 60s. But that was his audience. And I mean these guys was like anywhere from 18 to 60 years old. And the places where they performed, like the Café Wha? they recited poetry in those days as well as music. So he would have, a lot of times Sun Ra would have a poet. And Sun Ra would recite poetry as well. Even would sing. You know he would sing. And he was great. He was great. They just loved him. They just really loved him.
I just have this picture of you the next morning after a gig with him meeting someone for coffee and saying, “Man you should have seen what I did last night.”
